text: Becky Biberstein Michael Green Frances Carr Tom Richhart Troy Cook Bobbie Jackson Kimberly Abney Sydnee Bradburn Leanne Lee Mike Holland Matt Norris and Michael Abercrombie This weekend November 28 29 the Church enters into a new year of Gods grace and celebrates the First Sunday of Advent Though we begin a new liturgical year the theme of our readings seems familiar Last week we looked toward Christs coming at the end of time Today Advent keeps that expectation before us while also preparing us to celebrate His first coming into the world th th This season is often referred to as little Lent taking its familiar fourweek structure in the 9 Century Overall this preparatory and penitential season opens our hearts to the Lord who has come into the world Or in the words of the 4 Century Bishop of Hippo St Augustine To love His first coming so that we may be ready to rejoice at His second coming th th The Lord whom we await in glory at the end of time comes every day to knock at our door These words from Pope Leo for the First Sunday of Advent remind us of a simple Advent truth Christ comes to meet us each day inviting us to recognize His presence and welcome Him Advent invites us to notice the subtle changes that interrupt our routines and awaken us to the Lords coming Liturgically we encounter these subtle changes in both sight and sound During Advent the Gloria is not prayed save for solemnities This hymn of praise will not spring forth from our lips again until we join with that angelic choir that first broke the quiet of that silent night as they proclaimed Glory to God in the Higest to the shepherds in the field Our liturgical accouterments also face a subtle change Our gilded candlesticks and altar crucifix are switched with nearly identical wooden replacements The wood lacks that luster of the more precious metals Similarly the bleached candles are replaced with unbleached beeswax These elements provide a visual silence muted in color humble in appearance and showing the simplicity of Bethlehem ANNUAL ADVENT BABY SHOWER In preparation for the coming of the Christchild we will once again have the opportunity to help families in need Please see the display in the narthex this weekend for details on our annual Advent Baby Shower supporting The Closet this year The Closet provides free clothing diapers and necessities for Wells County families in need Thank you for supporting this good cause PARISH RENOVATIONS WHERE WE ARE AT As you can see half of our stencil work along the back of the sanctuary is now complete Rick Fischer of Deco Illusions will continue working on the back wall at the start of the New Year to avoid conflicting with our Advent or Christmas planning Likewise repair work on our woodworking with Shawnee Construction will also not begin until the New Year so as to work best with our parish schedule We will be meeting with Shawnee in December to discuss the order of work ECCE ADVENT LESSONS CAROLS We will welcome Ecce the Fort Wayne Young Adult Choir on Saturday December 12 at 2:30PM for a special Advent Lessons and Carols Program This liturgical service incorporates Scripture readings sacred music hymns and silence as a beautiful way for our parish community to enter more deeply into the spiritual meaning of Advent th Through the shared experience of sacred Word and music the service traces the biblical story of Gods promise of Salvation from humanitys longing for redemption to the prophetic expectation of the Messiah by the Angel Gabriel to the Blessed Virgin Mary and the hope fulfilled in the coming of Jesus Christ All are welcome to join us in this beautiful and prayerful service The liturgys central themes include Hope Waiting Light in Darkness Repentance and Preparation
